cards.card_text: Everything else, from the hide to the head, is burned on a wood fire outside the camp, at a ceremonially clean place on the ash heap.
cards.verse_text: But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, with its head and legs and its entrails and dung— all the rest of the bull—he must take outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place where the ashes are poured out, and there he must burn it on a wood fire on the ash heap.

cards.card_text: The priest puts on his linen robe and linen undergarments, removes the ashes from the altar and places them beside it, then changes into other clothes and carries the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.
cards.verse_text: Then he must take off his garments, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.
cards.snippet: …on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.

cards.card_text: After the priest makes atonement for her, the woman is ceremonially ___ from her flow of blood.
cards.verse_text: And the priest will present them before the LORD and make atonement for her; and she shall be ceremonially cleansed from her flow of blood.
cards.snippet: …before the LORD and make atonement for her; and she shall be ceremonially cleansed from her flow of blood.

cards.card_text: Next, the person washes his clothes, shaves off all his hair and bathes with water, and he's ceremonially clean.
cards.verse_text: The one being cleansed must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe with water; then he will be ceremonially clean.
cards.snippet: …off all his hair, and bathe with water; then he will be ceremonially clean.

cards.snippet: …of the heifer must also wash his clothes, and he will be ceremonially unclean until evening.

cards.card_text: Then a man who is ceremonially clean dips hyssop in the water and sprinkles the tent, its furnishings and the people who were there.
cards.verse_text: Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to take some hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the furnishings, and the people who were there.

cards.card_text: Moses says both the ceremonially clean and the ceremonially unclean may eat that everyday meat.
cards.verse_text: Both the ceremonially clean and unclean may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer,

cards.card_text: They eat that one within their gates, the ceremonially clean and unclean alike, but they don't eat the blood.
cards.verse_text: Eat it within your gates; both the ceremonially unclean and clean may eat it as they would a gazelle or a deer.

cards.verse_text: Saul said nothing that day because he thought, “Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.”
cards.snippet: …day because he thought, “Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.”

cards.card_text: The Gospel of Mark explains that some people don't eat until they wash their hands ceremonially, holding to the tradition of the elders.
cards.verse_text: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.
cards.snippet: …and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.

cards.card_text: Paul says that when they found him in the temple, he was ceremonially clean.
cards.verse_text: At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar.
cards.snippet: At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar.
